fields.title: Trajectory distillation: separate sampler, proposal, and divergence direction
fields.thesis: On-policy describes supervised states; FKL/RKL/JSD describe how distributions compare there. GKD and MiniLLM establish those axes, DrOPD and AP-OPD adjust correction location or strength, and Semi-OPD and learning-signal diagnostics distinguish offline reuse from residual loss. MPOPD adds a learnable proposal. Its geometric-mixture target differs from the student's teacher-directed RKL.
fields.axis_0: State source: teacher demonstrations, current student, or fixed initial-student trajectories
fields.axis_1: Comparison geometry: FKL coverage, RKL mode seeking, and JSD routing
fields.axis_2: Local treatment: add a correction direction or rescale existing supervision
fields.axis_3: Evidence type: objective, caching contract, or learning-signal diagnostic

fields.position: Lets the teacher supervise distributions at actual student-generated prefixes and mixes fixed with on-policy states through a student-data fraction.
fields.tradeoff: Better state coverage does not prescribe a divergence. The local candidate support does not reproduce T5 sequence training.

fields.position: Optimizes RKL on student generation with teacher-mixed sampling, baselines, and length treatment to stabilize estimates.
fields.tradeoff: Favors teacher modes the student can represent and can weaken undercovered directions. Local evidence verifies candidate sampling and gradient direction.

fields.position: Keeps RKL everywhere and adds FKL only at high-JS positions, using a PPO surrogate over the union of candidates.
fields.tradeoff: Supports teacher-probable candidates rarely sampled by the student, not a global switch to FKL. Full training was not reproduced; tiny online updates are L1 diagnostics.

fields.position: Compares raw penalties in neighboring blocks and scales all signed supervision in a block after a spike.
fields.tradeoff: No extra teacher forwards or sign change. Thresholds are not calibrated significance tests. Full runs were too costly and not reproduced.

fields.position: Freezes initial student trajectories and teacher scores but recomputes current student log-probabilities and advantages each step.
fields.tradeoff: Avoids repeated collection without covering all new states. The short-budget checkpoint verifies training flow only.

fields.position: Tracks residual loss, pre-truncation gradient, two-fold occupancy, parameter displacement, and CKA to distinguish loss from usable signal.
fields.tradeoff: A correlational diagnostic, not a new optimizer. The local three-step run does not recreate a long plateau or prove its cause.

fields.position: Fits a separate proposal to the normalized geometric mixture of updated student and teacher, while weighting student RKL on proposal trajectories by a frozen single-step ratio lagged one token.
fields.tradeoff: The ratio is not a cumulative product. Reset the proposal from the updated student each round. Complete sampling, LM copies, and optimizer orchestration are not implemented; tensor loss alone does not demonstrate on-policy training.

fields.title: Student trajectories can still support different learning directions
fields.body: GKD supervises prefixes students actually visit but permits multiple divergences. MiniLLM chooses student-to-teacher RKL, which may weakly correct teacher options with very low student support. DrOPD retains RKL and adds FKL only on high-divergence positions over joint candidate support. State sampling, divergence direction, and updated candidates need separate checks.

fields.title: Large loss, weak gradients, and spikes are not one fault
fields.body: OPD Learning Signals logs losses and gradients jointly rather than treating residual discrepancy as strong learning potential. AP-OPD scales whole blocks after abrupt penalty rises without changing signs; it does not explain plateaus generally. Semi-OPD changes state reuse; fixed teacher labels do not freeze student-dependent advantages.

fields.title: A new sampler does not make the geometric mixture the student target
fields.body: GKD supervises student prefixes and MiniLLM chooses student-to-teacher RKL. MPOPD keeps the teacher target but learns a separate proposal for reachability. The geometric mixture trains only the proposal. Correct sampling mismatch with the frozen old-student/old-proposal one-step ratio from the previous token, not a trajectory product. A real system must reset from the updated student each round; external logits alone do not establish trajectory provenance.

fields.question: Why add FKL in DrOPD if GKD and MiniLLM already learn along student trajectories?
fields.answer: Student trajectories determine prefixes only. MiniLLM RKL favors teacher modes the student supports, so low-probability teacher candidates can receive weak correction. DrOPD routes extra FKL at high-JS positions and retains teacher support. It does not change sampler or add unlimited FKL everywhere.
fields.example: Teaching example: A student considers only A at a visited mistaken prefix while a teacher favors B. Visiting the prefix does not guarantee a useful correction toward B.

fields.question: Why cache Semi-OPD teacher scores but not teacher-minus-student advantages forever?
fields.answer: Teacher configuration is fixed, but student parameters and log-probabilities change, so recompute differences. Stale advantages respond to old errors. Semi-OPD also fixes initial trajectories unlike continuously sampled GKD; neither implies all probabilities stay constant.
fields.example: Teaching example: An old teacher advantage can keep pushing a token the student has already learned.

fields.question: Are AP-OPD spike damping and DrOPD high-divergence FKL opposite corrections?
fields.answer: They detect different things. AP-OPD checks neighboring raw penalty blocks and scales all signed coefficients; DrOPD detects JS divergence and undercoverage and adds a direction. Strength and composition differ.
fields.example: Teaching example: Persistent high divergence with no jump can trigger DrOPD but not AP-OPD; their gates are not complementary thresholds.

fields.question: Should MPOPD distill the proposal's teacher–student mixture directly into the student?
fields.answer: No. The mixture shapes proposal sampling; the student still learns RKL to the teacher. Student loss uses a frozen old-student versus old-proposal single-step ratio with one-token lag. This adds a proposal axis beyond sampled states and divergence direction.
fields.example: Illustration: A proposal can reach a teacher-supported prefix more often without replacing the teacher target by a compromise.

fields.summary: Initial edition: separates student state distributions and divergence, comparing GKD/MiniLLM, DrOPD/AP-OPD, Semi-OPD, and learning-signal diagnostics; 40 abstracts and six close reads.

Reviewed MPOPD v2, separating proposal, student RKL, teacher top-k support, and the frozen single-step ratio lagged one token. Adds a learnable sampler axis beyond GKD/MiniLLM and preserves prerequisites such as proposal reset.
